## Purpose

This procedure describes the determination of compost maturity and
stability using the Solvita Compost Maturity Test (Woods End
Laboratories). The test simultaneously measures carbon dioxide (CO~2~)
and ammonia (NH~3~) emissions from a compost sample during a 4-hour
incubation, providing a dual indicator of biological activity and
nitrogen stabilization. The intersection of the two readings yields a
Compost Maturity Index (CMI) that indicates whether compost is immature,
active, curing, or finished [@vargas2005assessing].

CO~2~ evolution reflects ongoing microbial decomposition of organic
carbon. NH~3~ volatilization indicates incomplete nitrogen stabilization
and is associated with odor, phytotoxicity, and high pH. True compost
maturity is reached when both gases have declined to low levels. Because
the CO~2~ and NH~3~ cycles do not always track together, the
dual-measurement approach provides a more reliable maturity assessment
than either gas alone.

This SOP is distinct from
[SOP-L408 Solvita CO~2~ Burst](SOP-L408-solvita-co2-burst.qmd), which
measures rewetted *soil* respiration over 24 hours using only a CO~2~
paddle.


## Scope

- **Applies to:** Assessment of maturity and stability of composted
  organic materials, including green waste, food waste, biosolids
  compost, manure compost, and vermicompost
- **Does not apply to:** Soil respiration measurements (see
  [SOP-L408](SOP-L408-solvita-co2-burst.qmd)); raw feedstock
  characterization; long-term (7--28 day) laboratory respirometry;
  finished potting mixes where compost is a minor component
- **Location:** EA Program laboratory, SGM 133

## Definitions

- **Compost maturity:** A measure of how fully decomposed and stabilized a compost product is; mature compost no longer undergoes rapid decomposition, does not cause phytotoxicity, and can be safely applied to crops or soils.
- **CO~2~ index (Solvita):** The Solvita scale value (1--8) corresponding to the CO~2~ concentration in the headspace above moist compost; lower values indicate more active decomposition (less mature); higher values indicate stabilization.
- **Maturity index:** A combined score calculated from the CO~2~ and NH~3~ Solvita indices; the primary output of the Solvita compost maturity test; used by USCC, US Composting Council, and others to certify compost quality.
- **NH~3~ index (Solvita):** The Solvita scale value (1--5) corresponding to the NH~3~ concentration in the headspace above moist compost; high NH~3~ (low index) indicates immature compost with excess ammoniacal nitrogen that can harm plants.
- **Phytotoxicity:** Inhibition of plant germination or growth caused by immature compost; typically results from high NH~3~ concentrations, volatile fatty acids, or other metabolites produced during active decomposition.
- **Solvita paddle:** A plastic stick holding two gel-pad sensors (CO~2~ and NH~3~) inserted into the compost jar headspace during the test incubation; color changes are read with the Solvita DCR reader.


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Biological:** Compost may contain elevated microbial loads, fungal
  spores, and trace pathogens. Handle as a potential biohazard. Avoid
  inhaling dust when opening bags or scooping dry compost.
- **Chemical:** NH~3~ released from immature compost is an irritant at
  high concentrations. Work in a well-ventilated area when handling
  fresh or actively decomposing compost.
- **Physical:** Minor risk of glass breakage from incubation jars.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Nitrile gloves
- [ ] Safety glasses
- [ ] Lab coat
- [ ] Dust mask (recommended when handling dry or dusty compost)

### Emergency Procedures

If compost dust is inhaled and respiratory irritation occurs, move to
fresh air. For skin contact with compost, wash thoroughly with soap and
water. Refer to
[SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd).

| Item                          | Notes                                     |
|:------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|

| Solvita CMI Calculator spreadsheet | Available from Woods End / solvita.com for precise index calculation |


## Procedure

### Sample Collection and Preparation

1. Collect a representative compost sample of at least 500 g from the
   pile or windrow. Sample from the interior of the pile (at least 30 cm
   below the surface) to avoid surface drying artifacts.
2. If the compost is very heterogeneous, collect from multiple locations
   and composite the subsamples
3. The sample should be at "natural" moisture, not artificially wetted
   or dried. Compost that has been stored at 4 C should be brought to
   room temperature (20--25 C) before testing. Allow at least 30
   minutes.
4. Gently break up large clumps by hand but do not sieve or grind the
   compost. The test is designed for material in its as-produced
   condition.

::: {.callout-important}
Do not test compost that is above 40 C (i.e., still in the
thermophilic phase). Elevated temperatures accelerate gas production
and will give artificially high CO~2~ and NH~3~ readings that do not
reflect the maturity of the material once cooled.
:::

### Setting Up the Test

1. Fill a clean Solvita incubation jar loosely to the fill line with
   compost using the supplied scoop. Do not pack or compress the
   material. The volume should be approximately 150--200 mL.
2. Remove one CO~2~ gel paddle and one NH~3~ gel paddle from their
   sealed foil packets
3. Inspect each paddle: the gel should be uniform in color with no
   cracks, discoloration, or signs of prior exposure. Discard any
   compromised paddles.
4. Insert both paddles into the jar so that the gel faces are exposed to
   the headspace above the compost surface. The paddles should stand
   upright and not be buried in the compost.
5. Seal the jar immediately and securely
6. Record the jar number, sample ID, compost source, ambient
   temperature, and start time
7. Start the 4-hour timer

###  Incubation

1. Place sealed jars at room temperature (20--25 C) in a location
   shielded from direct sunlight and drafts
2. Do not open, move, or disturb jars during the 4-hour incubation

::: {.callout-note}
The standard incubation time is 4 hours. This is shorter than the
24-hour incubation used for the Solvita soil CO~2~ burst test
([SOP-L408](SOP-L408-solvita-co2-burst.qmd)) because compost produces
gas at much higher rates than soil.
:::

### Reading Results

1. After exactly 4 hours, open the jar and immediately remove both
   paddles
2. Read each paddle promptly. Prolonged exposure to ambient air will
   alter the gel color.

**Using the Solvita Color Charts (visual method):**

3. Compare the CO~2~ paddle to the Solvita CO~2~ color chart. Record
   the color number (1--8 scale, where 1 = highest CO~2~ / least
   stable, 8 = lowest CO~2~ / most stable).
4. Compare the NH~3~ paddle to the Solvita NH~3~ color chart. Record
   the color number (1--5 scale, where 1 = highest NH~3~ / least
   mature, 5 = lowest NH~3~ / most mature).

**Using the Solvita Digital Color Reader (DCR, recommended):**

3. Insert the CO~2~ paddle into the DCR and record the numerical
   reading
4. Insert the NH~3~ paddle into the DCR and record the numerical
   reading
5. The DCR values can be entered into the Solvita CMI Calculator
   spreadsheet for a more precise Maturity Index

### Determining the Compost Maturity Index (CMI)

Use the CO~2~ and NH~3~ color numbers to determine the CMI from the
Solvita lookup table (printed in the kit manual) or the CMI Calculator
spreadsheet:

| CMI | Interpretation            | Recommended Action              |
|:----|:--------------------------|:--------------------------------|
| 1   | Raw, very immature        | Continue active composting      |
| 2   | Immature, highly active   | Continue active composting      |
| 3   | Immature, active          | Continue composting/curing      |
| 4   | Moderately immature       | Begin curing phase              |
| 5   | Mid-range maturity        | Continue curing                 |
| 6   | Moderately mature         | Approaching readiness           |
| 7   | Mature                    | Ready for most applications     |
| 8   | Very mature, highly stable | Fully finished compost         |

::: {.callout-tip}
### Tip
Most regulatory agencies and compost quality programs consider a CMI of
6 or above as "mature" and suitable for unrestricted use. A CMI of 7--8
indicates a fully finished product with minimal phytotoxicity risk. For
sensitive applications (seed germination, potting mixes), target CMI 7
or 8.
:::

### Cleanup

1. Dispose of used compost in the designated waste container or return
   it to the compost pile
2. Wash incubation jars thoroughly with soap and water; rinse with
   deionized water and allow to air-dry
3. Dispose of used gel paddles in standard trash


## Quality Control and Acceptance Criteria

### QC Requirements

- Run duplicate tests on at least 10% of samples (two jars from the
  same homogenized compost). Duplicate CO~2~ readings should agree
  within 1 color number; NH~3~ readings within 1 color number.
- Include a blank jar (empty, sealed with both paddles) in each batch
  to check for ambient CO~2~ and NH~3~ interference. Both paddles
  should read at or near their maximum (most stable) values.
- Verify that the compost sample temperature is between 20 and 40 C
  before testing. Record the temperature.
- Calibrate the DCR per the manufacturer's instructions before each
  batch if using the digital reader.
- Store gel paddles sealed in their foil packets, at room temperature,
  away from light. Check expiration dates; do not use expired paddles.

### Complementary Tests

For a comprehensive compost quality assessment, consider pairing the
Solvita test with:

| Parameter                     | SOP / Method                              |
|:------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|
| pH and electrical conductivity | [SOP-L402](SOP-L402-soil-pH-salinity.qmd) (1:5 compost-water extract) |
| Moisture content               | [SOP-L400](SOP-L400-soil-moisture.qmd) (105 C, 24 h) |
| Organic matter (LOI)           | [SOP-L406](SOP-L406-loss-on-ignition.qmd)  |
| Total C and N (C:N ratio)      | [SOP-L407](SOP-L407-total-carbon.qmd) and elemental analysis |
| Seed germination bioassay      | *TBD*                                     |

## Training Record

Before performing the Solvita compost maturity test independently,
personnel must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Complete [SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd)
   training
3. Review the Solvita Compost Maturity Test User's Guide (included in
   the kit)
4. Observe a trained operator perform the full procedure from sample
   collection through CMI determination
5. Perform at least one test under supervision with acceptable duplicate
   precision (within 1 color number)
6. Be signed off by the PI or lab manager


## Appendix A: Solvita Compost Maturity Index Lookup Table {.appendix}

The following table reproduces the general structure of the Solvita CMI
lookup. Consult the kit manual or CMI Calculator spreadsheet for the
official version.

|            | **NH~3~ = 1** | **NH~3~ = 2** | **NH~3~ = 3** | **NH~3~ = 4** | **NH~3~ = 5** |
|:-----------|:------------:|:------------:|:------------:|:------------:|:------------:|
| **CO~2~ = 1** | 1         | 1            | 1            | 2            | 2            |
| **CO~2~ = 2** | 1         | 2            | 2            | 3            | 3            |
| **CO~2~ = 3** | 2         | 2            | 3            | 4            | 4            |
| **CO~2~ = 4** | 2         | 3            | 4            | 5            | 5            |
| **CO~2~ = 5** | 3         | 4            | 5            | 6            | 6            |
| **CO~2~ = 6** | 3         | 4            | 5            | 6            | 7            |
| **CO~2~ = 7** | 4         | 5            | 6            | 7            | 7            |
| **CO~2~ = 8** | 5         | 5            | 6            | 7            | 8            |

*Note: This table is approximate. Use the official Solvita color charts
and CMI Calculator for definitive results.*


## Appendix B: Interpreting Results in Context {.appendix}

### CO~2~ Color Number Interpretation

| Color No. | CO~2~ Level          | Stability Interpretation         |
|:----------|:---------------------|:---------------------------------|
| 1--2      | Very high            | Actively decomposing; unstable   |
| 3--4      | Moderate to high     | Active composting phase          |
| 5--6      | Low to moderate      | Curing; approaching stability    |
| 7--8      | Very low             | Stable; decomposition essentially complete |

### NH~3~ Color Number Interpretation

| Color No. | NH~3~ Level          | Maturity Interpretation          |
|:----------|:---------------------|:---------------------------------|
| 1         | Very high            | Strong odor; phytotoxic; immature |
| 2         | High                 | Significant ammonia; not ready   |
| 3         | Moderate             | Some ammonia; continue curing    |
| 4         | Low                  | Approaching maturity             |
| 5         | Very low / none      | Nitrogen stabilized; mature      |

### Common Patterns

| CO~2~ | NH~3~ | Interpretation                                    |
|:------|:------|:--------------------------------------------------|
| High  | High  | Actively decomposing with unstable N; classic immature compost |
| High  | Low   | Carbon-rich material still decomposing but N is stabilized; may need more time |
| Low   | High  | Unusual; possible anaerobic conditions or recent N-rich amendment; investigate |
| Low   | Low   | Both carbon and nitrogen cycles complete; finished compost |


## Appendix C: Troubleshooting {.appendix}

| Symptom                       | Probable Cause                  | Corrective Action              |
|:------------------------------|:--------------------------------|:-------------------------------|
| CO~2~ paddle reads 1 (max activity) after 4 h | Compost is very fresh or sample was too warm | Verify sample temperature was below 40 C; confirm composting has progressed past thermophilic phase |
| NH~3~ paddle reads 1 (max ammonia) | High free ammonia; fresh manure or urea input | Continue composting; ensure adequate C:N ratio (target 25:1--30:1) |
| Both paddles show no color change (max stability) | Compost is fully mature, or paddles expired | Verify paddle expiration date; confirm with a known immature sample |
| Duplicates disagree by more than 1 color number | Heterogeneous compost; inconsistent fill level | Homogenize sample more thoroughly; fill jars to consistent level |
| CO~2~ high but NH~3~ low | High-carbon, low-N material (e.g., wood chip compost) | Normal for C-rich substrates; continue composting until CO~2~ declines |
| CO~2~ low but NH~3~ high | Possible anaerobic pocket; recent N amendment | Turn the pile to aerate; reduce N inputs; retest in 1--2 weeks |
